answer: Shared-clock skew clustering. Each client leaks timing: TCP timestamps, drift, retry spacing. After the fact, a mixture model over per-identity drift estimates groups identities whose skews collide within measurement error — an echo of one machine under many names. Clusters past the population baseline get scored against a labelled sample (the opal audit set), then frozen, rewards clawed back. One network inlet's traffic runs it. Attacker cost: real hardware per identity, plus forfeiture per caught cluster.
